name: Ling-3.1-flash

lineage.how_derived: post-trained from the Ling-3.1-flash base; the card says it builds upon Ling-3.0-flash with improvements in architecture and performance (it is far larger: 560B total against 124B for Ling-3.0-flash, so not a continuation of those weights; the card does not say how the two relate)

purpose: The card presents an upgraded native hybrid reasoning model for complex real-world tasks: general-purpose agents, search, office productivity and software engineering, plus finance and materials science. inclusionAI also ships LingCode, a harness built on the open-source coding agent Pi for hours-long, hundreds-of-tool-call coding tasks.

license.name: MIT (card tag; no LICENSE file in the repository)
license.notes: Card YAML says mit; raw/main/LICENSE returns 404 (2026-11-19), so no licence text was read. The card links a training-content summary PDF that it says does not replace the licence.

architecture.kind: hybrid linear attention MoE (Kimi Delta Attention + gated MLA)
architecture.gguf_arch: bailing hybrid (config model_type bailing_hybrid, class BailingMoeV3ForCausalLM; llama.cpp support status per the quant repos not verified here)
architecture.attention: 63 KDA layers and 9 gated MLA layers (7:1), 64 heads, hidden 4096, 4 dense layers
architecture.drafter: MTP (num_nextn_predict_layers = 1; SGLang NEXTN and vLLM mtp with 3 speculative tokens in the card commands)
architecture.why_this_design: The card gives no reasons for the 7:1 ratio or the expert count. Note: config.json max_position_embeddings is 262144 with rope_scaling null, while the card text says a 1M-token window; the source of the 1M claim is not shown.

variants.format: safetensors, config says FP8 e4m3 block quantisation with BF16 modules (card repo 573.81 GB)

variants.notes: AD-IQ1_M 160.93, AD-IQ2_XXS 174.14, AD-IQ2_XS 198.22, AD-IQ2_M 218.08, AD-IQ3_XXS 256.39, AD-Q4_K_M 354.39, AD-Q8_0 600.85 GB (file sizes only, card not read)
non-expert body 9.79 GB plus about 1.5 GB per expert layer file; total not summed, card not read
also bertholomus 3.03 bpw and boxwrench 2.10 bpw EXL3 repos; sizes not measured

pc-12gb.notes: smallest quant 131.0 GB (IQ1_S) against about 60 GB (9.6 VRAM + 50 RAM)

pc-24gb.notes: 131.0 GB against 21.6 GB VRAM + about 82 GB RAM = 104 GB

pc-32gb.variant: bartowski IQ1_S 131.0 GB or IQ1_M 145.1 GB
pc-32gb.notes: 29.6 GB VRAM + 128 GB RAM = about 158 GB: IQ1_S 131.0 GB leaves about 27 GB for KV, states and the OS, IQ1_M 145.1 GB leaves about 13 GB; 1-bit quality of a 560B/25B model is unmeasured and 25B active parameters stream from RAM on every token

mac-64gb+.notes: 131 GB against about 52 GB GPU share on a 64 GB Mac; larger Macs not assessed

other: vLLM (custom branch, tool and reasoning parser ling3)
engine_support.notes: The card documents only SGLang on 8 H200 and vLLM on 8 GPUs; llama.cpp support was not checked.

strengths: Vendor claims strong results on GDPVal-AA V2.1, HealthBench Professional, FrontierSWE and Terminal-Bench 4.0 (card text; the score table is an image)
weaknesses: 560B total parameters: the smallest public quant is 131 GB
25B active parameters is heavy for CPU expert offload
soft.behavior: Recommended sampling temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20 with enable_thinking true (card).
best_for: agentic coding and office tasks on large servers
soft.maturity: inclusionAI (Ant Group) with an established Ling/Ring line (see ling-3.0-flash); repo created 2026-10-13.

tona_fit.reason: Out of reach for every class except a 1-bit file on the 32 GB VRAM + 128 GB RAM class (131 GB IQ1_S, quality unmeasured). The 3.0 generation (124B, 5.1B active, 77 GB Q4_K_M) is the practical Ling for our users; 3.1 gets 4.5 times the parameters. Revisit only if a measured 2-bit build under about 150 GB appears.
